nodes_source.source_quote: A series of simulation experiments based on real-world traffic data are conducted to evaluate the proposed approach.
nodes_source.description: Traffic data from a freeway connecting Qingdao and Huangdao, China, including video frames for vehicle location extraction and 10-minute traffic volumes used for simulation calibration.
nodes_source.reproducibility_rationale: The paper states that the data used to support the results are available from the corresponding author upon request.

nodes_process.source_quote: Vehicle locations from raw images are extracted to reconstruct visual representations in the DRL method
nodes_process.description: Extracts vehicle location points (xi, yi) from raw video frames to create position matrices mt. Includes zooming and down-sampling to a 4x512 pixel size.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3, generic tools used, key parameter (size) stated but extraction method for (xi, yi) is brief.

nodes_process.source_quote: we stack the matrices of consecutive N time steps to represent the state st
nodes_process.description: Stacks three consecutive observations (N=3) to represent the traffic state, capturing vehicle dynamics.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, stacking logic and N value are explicitly defined.

nodes_process.source_quote: The algorithm for training the ramp metering policy is presented in Algorithm 1.
nodes_process.description: Trains a CNN-based Q-network using multitask learning (predicting Q-value, speed, and queue length) with experience replay and a target network. Uses Adam optimizer and epsilon-greedy strategy.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, all hyperparameters and architecture details provided in Table 1 and Figure 7.

nodes_process.source_quote: The proposed method is evaluated in SUMO, an open-source microscopic traffic simulator
nodes_process.description: Evaluates the trained model in a SUMO simulation of a real-world freeway tunnel merge. Compares against no-control and PI-ALINEA baselines over 20 experiments.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, simulation environment, hardware, and scenario parameters fully specified.

nodes_process.source_quote: A perturbation analysis is conducted to evaluate the impact of information contained in video data.
nodes_process.description: Divides the control area into 8 subareas and removes information from each to test model sensitivity.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3, subarea division shown in Fig 15, but exact perturbation method (removal) is brief.

nodes_sink.description: Convergence of episode reward and mean travel time over 1 million training frames.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Training parameters and architecture specified; results follow from described DRL process.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 9: Vehicle travel times in the mainline.
nodes_sink.description: Time-series comparison of mainline travel times for no-control, PI-ALINEA, and DRL scenarios.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Simulation environment (SUMO) and input volumes provided; results are plausible aggregations.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Table 2: Mean vehicle travel times in 20 simulation experiments (s).

nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Detailed per-experiment data provided; methodology for simulation is well-defined.

nodes_sink.description: Spatio-temporal speed heatmaps for the three control scenarios along the mainline.
